title: Prostate cANcer graDe Assessment challenge development set
version_basis: Kaggle does not publish a semantic dataset version. This product pins the competition reference, its 2020 opening release, the official record snapshots retrieved on 2026-11-11, and the complete development inventory expected after authorized acquisition.
citation: Bulten, W. et al. Artificial intelligence for diagnosis and Gleason grading of prostate cancer: the PANDA challenge. Nature Medicine 28, 154-163 (2022). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-021-01620-2

access.instructions: Sign in to Kaggle, accept the prostate-cancer-grade-assessment competition rules, and acquire the files with an authorized account. Do not place credentials or source bytes in Git or public DVC storage.

rights.attribution: Cite the PANDA challenge paper when using the dataset.
rights.scope: Non-commercial attribution and share-alike terms apply to the PANDA dataset. Kaggle competition access terms also apply.

caveats: Training labels were not assigned by multiple pathologists, unlike all private-test and most public-test images.
Pathologists may disagree on Gleason and ISUP grades, so the development labels contain label noise.
Masks are missing for 100 development slides and may contain false-positive or false-negative regions.
Radboud and Karolinska masks use different annotation units and code systems and must not be treated as one native ontology.

identities.policy: Treat image_id as the publisher slide identity. Do not infer patient or case links from filenames, labels, tissue, or ordering.

interfaces.ownership: Downstream MIL, segmentation, and classification products reference these records and artifacts. They must not copy source bytes or add cohort, ontology, exclusion, or partition decisions here.

checksums.evidence_snapshots: Pinned in source_records and verified by the default metadata-only build.
checksums.authorized_artifacts: The explicit private index command hashes train.csv and every whole-slide and available mask artifact.
